metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Rhode Island(2026):Rules,Exemptions&Examples

description: Rhode Island has a statewide sales tax, but covered gold/silver bullion and many legal-tender and non-legal-tender coins are exempt. Jewelry is taxable.

Sales tax applies
Standard Rhode Island sales tax applies at checkout.
What's covered by the exemption
Gold and silver bullion; legal-tender and non-legal-tender coins
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Rhode Island.
Is gold and silver bullion exempt from sales tax in Rhode Island?
+
Yes. Rhode Island’s exemption is broad for covered gold and silver bullion.
Are coins taxed in Rhode Island?
+
Many legal-tender and non-legal-tender coins are exempt when they fall under the state’s covered coin rules.
Are numismatic coins taxable in Rhode Island?
+
Often no, if the coin-specific rule is met. Some numismatic treatment can depend on whether the item qualifies under the covered coin exemption.
Is precious-metal jewelry taxable in Rhode Island?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable even though covered bullion and many coin purchases are exempt.
